items.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I wound up in a band, an organized band, and led by a woman, Olga Burns.

ctx.x: No kidding. Did he have maybe a bigger sound or something?

Well maybe he was just a better salesman. But I think I was 15 years old then. But I went off to college, and after the first year of college I wound up in a band, an organized band, and led by a woman, Olga Burns. And we had a trombone player in that band that brought in some arrangements that Red Nichols had played, and he was a Miff Mole fan. And so I learned a few things. In fact, in that summer he came in with whatever the magazine was about music and entertainment, it said Bix Beiderbecke had died, and…
He’s looked on as almost a legend now, Bix. And so was he really popular in the 20s also? But you hadn’t heard of him really until he died. Is that right?
